Function: Host that reads the INA228 and writes the state file and UART
Operating voltage: 3.3 V on the header pins used here
Connection: pin 1 3.3 V, pin 6 GND, pin 3 SDA, pin 5 SCL, pin 8 TX, pin 10 RX
Verification: NVIDIA Jetson Nano Developer Kit User Guide DA_09402
Notes: I2C is /dev/i2c-1. UART is /dev/ttyTHS1. The INA228 is I2C only. Do not put pack voltage on a header pin. Do not power pins 2 and 4. Jetson power is outside this monitor

Manufacturer / model: Texas Instruments INA228 on a breakout, for example Adafruit INA228
Operating voltage: VS 2.7-5.5 V from Jetson pin 1; bus 0-85 V
Connection: sensor cable to J41 pins 1 6 3 5; IN+ IN- VBUS
Notes: Address 0x40 with A1 and A0 at ground. Pack current does not flow through the PCB

Manufacturer / model: select after max charge and discharge current are known
Connection: high-side in the battery positive lead
Notes: R < 163.84 mV / Imax. Value is not chosen in this repo

Function: Case for the INA228 board only
Connection: PETG or ABS, M2 lid screws, M3 flange screws, M2 for the INA228
Notes: Body 48.8 x 46.4 x 20.1 mm. With flanges 72.8 x 46.4 mm. See battery/enclosure/README.md

Function: I2C and 3.3 V from the Jetson to the INA228
Connection: pin 1 3.3 V, pin 6 GND, pin 3 SDA, pin 5 SCL
Notes: This is the sensor cable. It is not a UART cable

Connection: battery side IN+ and VBUS; load side IN-
Notes: Unfused. A short on these leads is a short-circuit risk the owner accepted. Not the power cable
